tour.overview:
In the 5th century BC, after defeating the Persians, Athens rebuilt the temples on its sacred rock under the leadership of Pericles. The Parthenon, completed in 438 BC and dedicated to the goddess Athena, became the symbol of classical Greece and of the democracy, philosophy and theatre that Athens gave the world. The Acropolis has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1987.

This private day explains the ancient city with a licensed archaeologist guide. You climb the Acropolis at opening time to see the Propylaea, the Parthenon, the Erechtheion and the temple of Athena Nike, then visit the Acropolis Museum, built over an ancient neighbourhood, where the original sculptures are displayed in natural light. After lunch in Plaka, you walk through the Ancient Agora, the marketplace and civic heart of Athens, and end at Syntagma Square for the changing of the guard.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 7 hours 30 minutes
• Start and end: your hotel in Athens or the cruise port of Piraeus
• Type: private tour with licensed guide, car and driver
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: moderate; about 6 km, with an uphill walk on slippery marble to the Acropolis

WHAT YOU SEE
• The Acropolis: the Propylaea, the Parthenon, the Erechtheion and the temple of Athena Nike.
• The Theatre of Dionysus and the Odeon of Herodes Atticus.
• The Acropolis Museum.
• Plaka and Anafiotika.
• The Ancient Agora, the Stoa of Attalos and the Temple of Hephaestus.
• The changing of the guard at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier.

WHY THIS WORKS
We enter the Acropolis at 8:00, when the light is soft and the rock is calm, and visit the museum in the hottest hours, so the outdoor sites are seen at their best.

WHO IT SUITS
First-time visitors to Athens, cruise passengers in Piraeus, families and anyone curious about ancient Greece.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
If you have seen Athens before, choose our Delphi or Cape Sounion tours.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
The Acropolis has very little shade and the marble paths are slippery: wear shoes with grip, a hat and bring water. In summer the site may close in the early afternoon during heatwaves. A lift serves the Acropolis for people with reduced mobility.

days.name: The Acropolis and the Parthenon, the Acropolis Museum, Plaka, the Ancient Agora and Syntagma Square
days.description:
What to expect: the monuments of classical Athens in one day, with a licensed archaeologist guide, private car, timed tickets and lunch.

Your driver collects you at your hotel or at the cruise terminal in Piraeus at about 7:30. Your guide meets you at the entrance on the south slope for the 8:00 opening. You climb past the Theatre of Dionysus, where the tragedies of Aeschylus, Sophocles and Euripides were first performed, and the Odeon of Herodes Atticus, still used for summer concerts, to the Propylaea, the monumental gateway of the rock.

On the summit stands the Parthenon, designed by the architects Ictinus and Callicrates and decorated under the direction of the sculptor Phidias. Your guide shows you the optical refinements that make it look perfect – its columns lean slightly inwards and swell in the middle, and no line is truly straight – and explains its long history as a temple, church, mosque and gunpowder store, blown up in 1687. Opposite, the Erechtheion, sacred to Athena and Poseidon, has its famous porch held up by six maidens, the Caryatids. You see the little temple of Athena Nike above the gateway and look out over Athens to the sea.

At about 10:30 you walk down to the Acropolis Museum, opened in 2009. Its glass floors show the excavated streets beneath, and on the top floor the Parthenon frieze is displayed in its original order, the missing pieces held in London shown as casts. You see the original Caryatids, cleaned by laser, and the archaic statues of young women, the korai, still bearing traces of paint.

Lunch is in a taverna in Plaka, the old district under the Acropolis – grilled octopus, moussaka, souvlaki and Greek salad. In the afternoon you walk through the Ancient Agora, the marketplace and political centre of Athens, where Socrates questioned his fellow citizens and Saint Paul preached. You see the reconstructed Stoa of Attalos, now a museum, and the Temple of Hephaestus, the best-preserved Doric temple in Greece. Your driver takes you to Syntagma Square to watch the evzones, the presidential guards in their kilts and pompom shoes, change guard at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier, then back to your hotel or ship at about 15:00.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
07:30 – Pick-up at your hotel or the port.
08:00 – The Acropolis (about 2 hours).
10:30 – The Acropolis Museum (about 1 hour 30 minutes).
12:15 – Lunch in Plaka.
13:30 – The Ancient Agora and the Temple of Hephaestus.
14:30 – Syntagma Square and the changing of the guard.
15:00 – Back at your hotel or ship.

GOOD TO KNOW
• The guard changes every hour; on Sundays at 11:00 there is a larger ceremony with the band.
• Large bags are not allowed on the Acropolis.
• Cruise passengers: we plan to have you back at the ship at least one hour before all-aboard time.

INCLUDED: private car and driver, licensed guide, Acropolis, Acropolis Museum and Ancient Agora tickets, lunch, bottled water, pick-up and drop-off.
NOT INCLUDED: drinks with lunch, tips.

Overnight: none.
Meals: lunch.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: Do we skip the lines at the Acropolis?
faq.answer: We book timed tickets for the 8:00 opening slot, so you avoid the ticket queue. There is a short wait at the entrance gate at busy times.

faq.question: Are the entrance tickets included?
faq.answer: Yes: the Acropolis, the Acropolis Museum and the Ancient Agora.

faq.question: Is it very hot?
faq.answer: From June to September the Acropolis is very hot and has almost no shade, which is why we start at opening time. During heatwaves the site may close between noon and 17:00.

faq.question: Is there much walking?
faq.answer: About 6 km, including the climb to the Acropolis on uneven, slippery marble. The car takes you between the sites when it helps.

faq.question: Is lunch included?
faq.answer: Yes, lunch at a taverna in Plaka. Vegetarian, gluten-free and other diets can be arranged.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes. Children enjoy the myths of Athena and Poseidon, the guards' march and the glass floors of the museum.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: Partly. A lift on the north side of the Acropolis serves visitors with reduced mobility, though the summit is uneven. The museum is fully accessible. Tell us your needs.

faq.question: Can you pick us up from the cruise ship?
faq.answer: Yes. We meet you at the cruise terminal in Piraeus, about 30 minutes from the Acropolis, and plan the day around your ship's times.

faq.question: Can we take photos?
faq.answer: Yes, on the Acropolis and in most of the museum. Posing photos on the monuments, such as sitting on the marble, are not allowed.

faq.question: What should we wear?
faq.answer: Shoes with good grip, a hat, sunglasses and sun cream. Heels are not allowed on the Acropolis.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: April to June and September to October. Winter is mild and much quieter; summer is very hot.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 24 hours before the tour. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
